narrative: Material PL1__M7609E01 displays smooth, stationary daily demand (CV=0.268) with no detectable trend across the 85-observation window from March 2025 to March 2026. However, supplier lead times are highly unstable (CV=1.09, σ=1.75 days), driving 67.5% of total demand-during-lead-time variance and necessitating a safety stock of 2,327 units to achieve the 95% service level target. An (r,Q) fixed-reorder-point policy is recommended, with EOQ set at 7,674 units — well above the MOQ of 1,675 — to minimize total ordering and holding costs, yielding an estimated annual saving of $2,823 vs. the current SAP policy.

research_insights.selected_model: (r, Q) — Fixed Reorder Point, Fixed Order Quantity (EOQ-based)
research_insights.selection_rationale: Demand is smooth and continuous (CV=0.268), making the classical (r,Q) model appropriate. The fixed reorder point handles the high lead-time variability through the safety stock buffer, while the EOQ order quantity minimizes total replenishment and holding costs. An (s,S) or periodic-review policy would add unnecessary complexity without improving performance for this demand pattern.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Storage capacity of 10,692 units is respected: safety_stock (2,327) + order_quantity (7,674) = 10,001 units, leaving a 690-unit buffer (6.5% headroom). No capacity cap binds. If safety stock requirements increase or demand surges, the remaining headroom is limited and should be monitored.
